catalog_quote: [StressTyp2 passage 1975, Reesink 1987:39] Stress in usan cannot be predicted. Each grammatical word may receive primary stress. Polysyllabic words in context cannot obscure their inherent stress. Monosyllabic words have their stress reduced considerably when the primary stress of a stress group is assigned somewhere else. Stress also plays a role in the morphology. ... [Pick 2020:31-32] On the other hand, Reesink (1987: 39-40) characterizes stress in Usan as phonemic, and illustrates this with minimal pairs that differ only in stress, such as [go.ˈbi] 'a tree', and [ˈgo.bi] 'taro seedling'. ... [fn.11] Reesink does not make clear whether in Usan stress placement generally follows certain patterns, but has exceptions, as in Pamosu, or whether it is completely unpredictable. ... new_statements.relation_note: The catalog record (src gordon) gives Usan a fixed penultimate rule (penultimate stress). Pick, citing the primary grammar Reesink 1987: 39-40, says Usan stress is phonemic and contrastive, with a disyllabic minimal pair contrasting initial and final stress; under a fixed: penultimate syllable rule 'go.ˈbi' with final stress could not exist. So the type differs (lexical/contrastive vs fixed: penultimate syllable), not just the placement. Note that Pick's statement is second-hand (relayed from Reesink), and he explicitly leaves open whether a default pattern exists.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress in Usan is phonemic (contrastive): its position distinguishes words, as in the disyllabic minimal pair go.ˈbi 'a tree' (final stress) vs ˈgo.bi 'taro seedling' (initial stress). Pick relays this from Reesink (1987: 39-40) and adds that Reesink does not make clear whether there is a general default pattern with exceptions or complete unpredictability. Pick has no stress data of his own for Usan (he states he has 'little else to say about stress in Northern Adelbert languages', p. 32) and his Usan wordlists do not mark stress.
new_statements.exceptions: None for Usan beyond the note (fn. 11) that it is unclear whether stress follows a general pattern with exceptions. Pick's comparative remarks: Mauwake has predictable second-syllable stress (Berghäll 2015: 42); Pamosu has final stress on closed final syllables and antepenultimate stress on open final syllables with numerous exceptions (Tupper 2012: 99-102) — these are other Northern Adelbert languages, not Usan.
new_statements.identity_note: Pick 2020 treats Usan proper (Reesink 1987's language, Numugen subgroup of Northern Adelbert, ISO wnu, Wanuma area of Madang; Reesink estimated 1,400 speakers). No dialect is singled out; all of Pick's Usan phonology/grammar information is taken from Reesink (1987, n.d.) and Z'graggen (1975, 1980b), and Pick collected no Usan stress data himself. The Mauwake and Pamosu stress statements in the same subsection are about other Northern Adelbert languages.

readall_conflicts: One conflict. The catalog's Gordon-sourced record gives Usan fixed penultimate stress (penultimate stress). The only open work listed, Pick 2020 (pp. 32, 421), relays Reesink 1987: 39-40 as characterising Usan stress as phonemic, with the minimal pair [go.ˈbi] 'a tree' vs [ˈgo.bi] 'taro seedling', i.e. contrastive/lexical stress rather than a fixed penultimate rule. Pick's footnote 11 leaves open whether Reesink's description hides a default pattern with exceptions. 39 reads 'Stress in Usan cannot be predicted. It is therefore phonologically significant', p. 88 mentions a morphological restriction (no word stress on the syllable containing the future-tense morpheme unless it is heavy), and records WALS 14A/15A/16A for Usan as No fixed stress / Not predictable / Lexical stress (source Reesink 1987). The primary source, Reesink 1987 ch. 2 pp. 25-42, is paywalled (Benjamins) and was not opened; the basis of the Gordon penult entry should be checked against it before the catalog is changed.

audit.reasoning: The classification (lexical/unpredictable stress, no weight conditioning, no secondary stress described) rests on the phonology chapter of the only reference grammar of Usan (Reesink 1987:39-40), which is the best available description; no later phonology or instrumental study exists in Glottolog or could be found. The quotation is verified verbatim in the held StressTyp2 database (passage 1975, p.39) and independently corroborated by Pick 2020 (held PDF, pp.31-32, fn.11, ch.10) with stress-only minimal pairs, and by WALS's independent reading of Reesink 1987 (No fixed stress / Lexical). Nothing suggests the classification is wrong; the record's own correction of Gordon 2002 and StressTyp2-SPD 'penult' is sound (goˈbi vs ˈgobi falsifies fixed penult at length 2). It is not 'well-sourced' only because pp.39-40 of the primary are not yet obtained and were read through carriers; obtaining Reesink 1987 ch.2
